claim.quote: We present measurements of the temperature and E-mode polarization angular power spectra of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) from observations of 4% of the sky with SPT-3G, the current camera on the South Pole Telescope (SPT).

date.note: arXiv v1 submission date; the journal publication date was not read from a fetched source.

key_value_text.quote: We report a Hubble constant of $H_0=66.66\pm0.60$ km/s/Mpc from SPT-3G alone, 6.2 sigma away from local measurements from SH0ES.
key_value_text.value: H0 = 66.66 ± 0.60 km/s/Mpc from SPT-3G alone, 6.2σ from local (SH0ES) measurements; 67.19 ± 0.38 from SPT+ACT+Planck

name: SPT-3G D1: CMB temperature and polarization power spectra and cosmology from 2019 and 2020 observations of the SPT-3G Main field

official_url.quote: SPT-3G D1: CMB temperature and polarization power spectra and cosmology from 2019 and 2020 observations of the SPT-3G Main field

summary.plain: The South Pole Telescope's SPT-3G camera produced the deepest maps yet used for a full temperature-and-polarization analysis of the Big Bang afterglow. Alone it gives a Hubble constant of 66.7, in tension with local measurements.
summary.technical: SPT-3G D1 (2019-2020 Main field, 4% of sky): TT/TE/EE spectra; LCDM parameters consistent with Planck and ACT-DR6; H0 = 66.66 +/- 0.60 km/s/Mpc (6.2 sigma from SH0ES); SPT+ACT+Planck H0 = 67.19 +/- 0.38, sigma_8 = 0.8137 +/- 0.0037; 2.8 sigma CMB-DESI DR2 BAO difference in LCDM.

title: SPT-3G D1: CMB temperature and polarization power spectra and cosmology from 2019 and 2020 observations of the SPT-3G Main field
why_it_matters: The abstract says that for the first time "combined ground-based (SPT+ACT) CMB primary and lensing data have reached Planck's constraining power on some parameters, a milestone for CMB cosmology".
